uno.hex_span_expected_note: hex_span_expected (the single flat value above) is arm-AGNOSTIC for a quantity that is genuinely arm-DEPENDENT -- measured, from images/BUILD-MANIFEST.json: control's uno hex_span is 26026 B, v133's is 22952 B (~3 KB apart; see BUILD-MANIFEST.json measured_divergence_finding for the full root-cause chain -- PR #55's VPE-settle amortisation grew flash by +478 B on uno with its own size_baseline.json re-record deliberately deferred, and Phase 158's size reduction then landed only on the v1.33 side). The flat value happens to equal v133's own span and would silently reject a correctly-flashed control-arm read-back as 'not the artifact the manifest describes'. hex_span_expected_by_arm is the authoritative, arm-aware replacement judge_readback.py's cross_check_hex_span() now consults first (keyed by --expect-arm); hex_span_expected is kept, unedited, only for backward compatibility with any reader that still consults the flat key directly. Found and fixed in 160-08 as a Rule 2 deviation (a pinned constant that is arm-agnostic for an arm-dependent quantity) -- 160-09/160-10 will hit the identical field shape for uno328pb/leonardo.

uno328pb.hex_span_expected_note: Same arm-dependence defect as targets.uno.hex_span_expected_note (measured from BUILD-MANIFEST.json: control=26074 B, v133=23000 B). Fixed here in 160-08 alongside the uno entry so plan 09 inherits a correct value rather than re-discovering the same gap; plan 09 must still resolve judged_span_policy's own PENDING-xshowvector placeholder separately -- that is a different field, untouched by this fix.
uno328pb.judged_span_policy_note: Deliberate placeholder. Plan 09 replaces this with a policy derived from the recorded `-xshowvector` output (Pitfall 3: urclock may patch the reset vector + one interrupt vector on a vector bootloader, producing a false RED at 0x0000 on every flash). Every tool must refuse to judge this target while this value is still PENDING-xshowvector.

vector_exclusions.reason: reset vector (vector 0): urclock's -xshowvector reported this bootloader is a VECTOR bootloader (vector 25, SPM_Ready); measured live on the control-arm flash (BRINGUP-uno328pb/BOOTLOADER.md): expected bytes 0c 94 cf 01, actual (post-flash read-back) 3f cf 75 72 -- all 4 bytes of this JMP-encoded vector slot differ, as expected since urclock redirects RESET into the urboot bootloader

designated interrupt vector 25 (SPM_Ready), the vector -xshowvector named; offset = vector_number * 4 bytes (JMP-based vector table, RESET=vector 0) = 25*4 = 100, measured live: expected bytes 0c 94 f7 01, actual 0c 94 cf 01 -- 1 of 4 bytes differs (offset 102), because urclock stores a copy of the application's original reset target in this slot

leonardo.hex_span_expected_note: Same arm-dependence defect as targets.uno.hex_span_expected_note (measured from BUILD-MANIFEST.json: control=28170 B, v133=25098 B). Fixed here in 160-08 alongside uno/uno328pb so plan 10 inherits a correct value.
leonardo.chip_out_before_sideload_note: Leonardo is exempt — flashed with the chip seated (standing memory: chip-out-before-sideload is Uno-class only).
leonardo.measured_post_touch_port_behavior_note: Measured live, 160-10 Leonardo bring-up (BOOTLOADER-WINDOW.md): two independent 1200-baud touch cycles on this exact board both found devices_before == devices_after == ['/dev/ttyACM0'] -- Caterina returns on the SAME node the application uses, never a new one. This matches the historical avr_tool.py write-direction observation (.planning/debug/resolved/fw-update-blocked-release-fw.md:283, a 5.51s avr109 session on the same node) and is now also measured, independently, for the READ direction. touch_1200.py's --wait-new-port mode was tried first (per this plan's own instruction not to assume) and empirically timed out after 3s with the node list unchanged -- it is the WRONG mode for this board and is not used on the working chain; the bare (settle-only, reuse --port) mode is.
leonardo.measured_touch_to_read_complete_s_note: Elapsed wall-clock from the 1200-baud touch's own open/close call to judge_readback.py's completed, judged_match=true verdict for the control arm's full 32768 B read-back (avrdude's own read itself took only 0.31s once started -- see BRINGUP-leonardo/BOOTLOADER-WINDOW.md). Comfortably inside the roughly-8s Caterina inactivity window RESEARCH.md Pitfall 5 describes, with continuous communication throughout so the inactivity timer never had a gap to fire against.

chips_note: The nine new chips entries (w27e512, sst27sf512, fm1608, w27e040, sst39sf040, w29c040, am27c020, m27c512, 2516) were derived from the v1.33 arm's own EpromDatabase by a one-shot script run on 2026-08-28 (.planning/v1.34/bench/cells/CHIP/CHIPS-MAP-DERIVATION.md carries the exact command, verbatim output, and a cross-check against RESEARCH R7's independently-measured table -- no field is hand-typed). stamp_width is deliberately absent on all nine: it is gen_addr_image.py's address-stamp width for a generated WRV image and has no meaning for a dev-test chip-sweep position that generates no image; it is present only on the two pre-existing WRV entries (w27c512, w29c020), which are otherwise byte-unchanged inputs to Phase 161's twelve recorded positions. chip_token is case-sensitive on every entry -- it is the exact CLI token typed at `dev test <TOKEN>`, and _sanitize_chip_token (cli_handlers.py) preserves case, so the report filename dev-test-<TOKEN>.json depends on the token's case exactly as recorded here. 2516 is present for inventory completeness under D-14 as a named absence: it is never seated, read, or written in this phase. family_label (added 162-02) is present on all eleven entries -- see chips_family_label_source.
chips_family_label_source: family_label on every chips[*] entry is looked up by algorithm -> hex bucket ("0x%02X" % algorithm) against .planning/v1.16/ledger/PROTOCOL-LEDGER.json's rows[*].bucket -> rows[*].proposed_name table (the six v1.16 PROTOCOL-LEDGER bucket names this milestone's eleven parts actually use: EPROM-STD, EPROM-QUICK, EPROM-LEGACY, FLASH-AMD-STD, FLASH-AMD-ALT, SRAM-STD), never a two-part literal duplicated inside a tool. Added in 162-02 as a Rule 2 deviation: append_chip_evidence.py's family column is prohibited from carrying its own chip-slug-to-label dictionary literal (the append_evidence.py _CHIP_LABEL pattern this sibling must not copy), and rig-pins.json's chips map had no label field for the appender to read. All 11 entries covered; FM1608's algorithm 40 (0x28) resolves to SRAM-STD, matching PROTOCOL-LEDGER.md's own NAME-04 correction of v1.15 EVIDENCE.md's stale '0x40 (SRAM_STD / FRAM)' label.
